findings.title: Severe Operating and Net Profit Contraction Masked by FY2024 Impairment Reversal
findings.description: Profit before tax fell by 27.3% from R5,155 million in FY2024 to R3,749 million in FY2025, and headline EPS fell 28.8% from 1,046.9 cents to 745.2 cents. While FY2024 benefited from a non-recurring R1,019 million intangible asset impairment reversal, core underlying trading profit still declined 9.6% (from R3,199 million pre-reversal in FY2024 to R2,892 million in FY2025) as trading expense growth outpaced merchandise sales growth.
findings.source_section: Group Statements of Comprehensive Income
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: Intangible asset impairment reversal - (2024: 1,019); Trading profit 2,892 (2024: 4,218); Profit before tax 3,749 (2024: 5,155); Basic earnings per share (cents) 745.2 (2024: 1,046.9)
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: operating_margin, pbt_growth, eps_growth
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Normalize historical operating margins by stripping out the FY2024 R1,019m impairment reversal to avoid overly optimistic baseline forecasts and recognize underlying trading profit margin compression.

findings.title: Full Concentration of Interest-Bearing Debt into Current Liabilities
findings.description: Non-current interest-bearing borrowings fell to R0 (down from R268 million in 2024), shifting 100% of interest-bearing term debt (R1,479 million) into current liabilities maturing within 12 months. When combined with bank overdrafts of R975 million and current lease liabilities of R1,045 million, the Group faces short-term debt refinancing/settlement requirements of nearly R3.5 billion.
findings.source_section: Group Statements of Financial Position
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: Interest-bearing borrowings [Non-current liabilities] - (2024: 268); Interest-bearing borrowings [Current liabilities] 1,479 (2024: 1,208); Bank overdraft 975 (2024: 1,099)
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: debt_maturity_profile, short_term_liquidity, refinancing_spread
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Verify refinancing negotiations, debt rollover terms, bank facility renewal conditions, and interest rate step-ups in subsequent notes (Note 16).

findings.title: Substantial Expected Credit Loss Allowance on Unsecured Consumer Book
findings.description: The Group carries significant credit risk on its unsecured consumer book, requiring total ECL allowances of R1,739 million across active (R1,339 million allowance against R6,448 million book, or 20.8%) and charged-off portfolios (R400 million allowance against R543 million book, or 73.7%). Annual net bad debt and ECL charges consumed R1,164 million, representing over 40% of Group trading profit.
findings.source_section: Independent Auditor's Report - Key Audit Matter
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: As at 29 June 2025 the Group’s trade receivables active portfolio amounted to R6 448 million, against which an ECL allowance of R1 339 million has been raised. The “charged-off” trade receivables portfolio... amounted to R543 million, against which an ECL allowance of R400 million was raised.
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: credit_loss_ratio, bad_debt_expense, trade_receivables_carrying_value
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Stress test receivables collections under sustained high-interest-rate scenarios in South Africa and assess sensitivity of the Markov model forward-looking overlays.

findings.title: Failure of Expected South African Macro Growth Tailwinds
findings.description: Management concedes that the anticipated macro recovery in South Africa following the May 2024 elections and the formation of the GNU failed to materialize due to internal coalition frictions and geopolitical/tariff headwinds, keeping consumer spending highly constrained despite two-pot retirement fund withdrawals.
findings.source_section: Directors' Report - Operating Context
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: However, much of this optimism failed to materialise due to a combination of geopolitical uncertainties - particularly around tariffs and rising tensions in the Middle East - and internal challenges within the GNU. Consequently, South Africa’s macroeconomic environment remained constrained
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: same_store_sales_growth, revenue_growth_south_africa
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Temper FY2026-FY2027 top-line volume growth assumptions for the Truworths Africa segment, treating GNU tailwinds as unproven.

findings.title: Cost Growth Outpacing Revenue Generating Negative Operating Leverage
findings.description: Merchandise sales grew by only 3.19% (from R20,664 million to R21,323 million), while other operating expenses increased by 11.17% (from R1,593 million to R1,771 million), occupancy costs climbed 6.81% (from R1,072 million to R1,145 million), and finance costs rose 10.29% (from R476 million to R525 million).
findings.source_section: Group Statements of Comprehensive Income
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: Sale of merchandise 21,323 (2024: 20,664); Occupancy costs (1,145) (2024: (1,072)); Other operating costs (1,771) (2024: (1,593)); Finance costs (525) (2024: (476))
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: opex_growth_rate, operating_margin, cost_to_income_ratio
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Review detailed notes on other operating expenses (Note 27.6) and occupancy costs (Note 27.4) to determine the structural vs discretionary drivers of this inflationary creep.

findings.title: 100% of Interest-Bearing Borrowings Classified as Current with Heavy Reliance on Uncommitted Overdraft
findings.description: All interest-bearing borrowings totaling R1,479 million are now classified as current liabilities (up from R1,208 million in FY2024), leaving zero non-current borrowings. This includes the fully drawn R1.2 billion revolving credit facility (subject to 12 months' cancellation notice) and the R268 million green term loan maturing in December 2025. Furthermore, the Group operates with net cash and cash equivalents of negative R11 million (due to a R975 million overdraft), drawing on a R2 billion banking facility where R1.7 billion is entirely uncommitted by lenders.
findings.source_section: Note 16: Interest-Bearing Borrowings & Note 12: Cash and Cash Equivalents
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: Non-current portion of interest-bearing borrowings - 268 / Current portion of interest-bearing borrowings 1,479 1,208 ... The SA Rand-based interest-bearing borrowings comprise of an unsecured variable-rate 12-month notice revolving credit facility (RCF) of R1.2 billion ... and is repayable in December 2025 ... At the period-end this facility was fully drawn ... The bank overdraft forms part of a South African Rand-based general short-term banking facility of R2 billion, of which R300 million is committed and R1.7 billion is uncommitted
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Short-term debt refinancing risk, liquidity ratios, net interest expense forecast
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Stress-test liquidity assuming lenders review or terminate the R1.7bn uncommitted facility, and model the refinancing terms and rates for the R268m green loan due December 2025 and the R1.2bn RCF.

findings.title: Inventory Shrinkage and Write-offs Doubled While Provision Coverage Decreased
findings.description: Inventory shrinkage and write-offs charged directly to cost of sales surged by 102.3% from R43 million in FY2024 to R87 million in FY2025. In contrast, the balance sheet allowance for markdown and shrinkage was reduced from 15.3% to 13.6% of gross inventory (and from 16.1% to 14.2% of finished goods), despite ongoing macro pressure and elevated clearance risks.
findings.source_section: Note 10: Inventories
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: * During the reporting period inventory shrinkage and write offs to the value of R87 million (June 2024: R43 million) were expensed in cost of sales. Please refer to note 27.1. / Allowances as a % of gross inventories (%) 13.6 15.3
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Gross profit margin, inventory write-down assumptions, cost of sales
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Scrutinize whether the 170 bps release in inventory provision percentage unsustainably protected reported gross margin against the backdrop of doubled in-store losses and stock leakage.

findings.title: Office UK Operational Slowdown Post Massive Historical Trademark Write-back
findings.description: In FY2024, management reversed R1,019 million of prior trademark impairments for Office UK, leaving trademark carrying value at R1,398 million in FY2025. However, detailed notes acknowledge that Office UK experienced marked pressure on operating expense growth and deceleration in sales growth in 2H2024, compounded by the cost-of-living crisis and expiration of energy/rates subsidies. The valuation discount rate applied remains very high at 19.3%, reflecting heightened vulnerability to any future top-line miss.
findings.source_section: Note 5: Intangible Assets - Office UK segment
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: However, there was notable pressure on expense growth rates and a decline in sales growth rates during the second half of the 2024 reporting period, as the macro environment remains volatile and uncertain in light of the UK economic challenges and the continued decline in consumer spending on the back of the ongoing cost of living crisis.
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Office UK operating profit, intangible asset impairment sensitivity, medium-term revenue CAGR
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Assess impairment headroom for the R1.4bn Office trademark under a scenario of negative UK retail volume growth and rising store wage inflation.

findings.title: Sharp Spike in Truworths Africa Right-of-Use Asset Impairments and Extended Debtor Days
findings.description: Store profitability deterioration in the Truworths Africa segment triggered R35 million of right-of-use (ROU) asset impairments in FY2025, nearly triple the R12 million recognized in FY2024. Simultaneously, debtor days remain exceptionally extended at 230 days, with R335 million of charged-off accounts utilized (derecognized/written off) compared to only R56 million in FY2024.
findings.source_section: Note 3: Right-of-Use Assets & Note 11: Trade and Other Receivables
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: Impairment of right-of-use assets (35) (12) / Truworths Africa segment (35) (12) ... The debtors’ days at the reporting date were 230 days (2024: 229 days) ... Allowance utilised (335) (56)
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Store footprint rationalization, retail credit credit-loss provisions, working capital velocity
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Evaluate store-level ROIC in South Africa to estimate future store closure/impairment costs and evaluate ECL coverage sufficiency given the 230-day collection cycle.

findings.title: Prior-Period Classification Errors Restated Between FVTPL and FVOCI
findings.description: Management disclosed a balance sheet reclassification and correction of errors in financial asset presentation: assets previously reported at fair value through other comprehensive income (FVOCI) were incorrectly classified and have been restated to fair value through profit or loss (FVTPL), alongside reclassifying lease liabilities from other financial liabilities to amortised cost.
findings.source_section: Note 25.1: Financial Risk Management - Classifications
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: * We have updated the presentation of lease liabilities from other financial liabilities to liabilities at amortised cost. In addition, we have restated assets which were incorrectly presented at fair value through other comprehensive income to assets held at fair value through profit or loss in the current financial period
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Statement of Comprehensive Income line-item volatility, classification integrity
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Verify whether fair value movements in these restated assets will introduce recurring volatility into headline operating profit and EPS.

findings.title: Severe Margin Compression and Stagnation in Core Truworths Africa Segment
findings.description: While group headline revenue grew slightly (+2.8%), Truworths Africa (which generates ~67% of Group revenue and 70% of sales on credit) stagnated in revenue and suffered severe operational deleverage. Third-party revenue contracted from R15,428m to R15,415m and sale of merchandise rose just 0.3% to R13,770m. Gross margin contracted by 130 bps (from 54.9% to 53.6%), trading margin dropped 220 bps (from 13.3% to 11.1%), and segmental operating margin dropped 270 bps (from 23.1% to 20.4%). Segment profit for the period dropped 16.2% from R2,045m to R1,714m.
findings.source_section: Note 35.1 Reportable segment information
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: Truworths Africa: Total third party revenue 15,415 (2024: 15,428) ... Gross margin (%) 53.6 (2024: 54.9) ... Trading margin (%) 11.1 (2024: 13.3) ... Operating margin (%) 20.4 (2024: 23.1) ... Profit for the period 1,714 (2024: 2,045)
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Truworths Africa revenue growth, segment trading margin, and operating leverage assumptions
findings.recommended_analyst_review: De-couple Truworths Africa and Office UK in financial projections. Adjust medium-term operating margins downward for Africa, reflecting rising domestic retail competition, pressured consumer disposable income, and higher structural store operating costs.

findings.title: Surging In-Period Bad Debt Write-offs and Doubling of Inventory Shrinkage
findings.description: Underlying credit risk and operational loss indicators deteriorated noticeably during FY2025. Amounts written off in respect of trade receivable balances originating in the current period surged by 94.0% from R183 million in FY2024 to R355 million in FY2025. Total Stage 3 ECL provision coverage on active trade receivables escalated from 64.3% to 67.7%, and overall trade receivables provision coverage reached 24.9% (2024: 24.6%). Simultaneously, inventory shrinkage and write-offs in cost of sales more than doubled (+102.3%) from R43 million to R87 million.
findings.source_section: Note 27.5 Trade receivable costs and Note 27.1 Cost of sales
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: Inclusive of R251 million (2024: R263 million) of bad debt recoveries and debt sold, and amounts written-off of R355 million (2024: R183 million) in respect of balances arising in the current period. ... Shrinkage and write-offs 87 (2024: 43)
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Credit loss write-off rate, trade receivable provisioning rate, and gross margin shrink drag
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Scrutinize vintages of recent account originations. A doubling of year-1 credit defaults suggests credit score cuts or aggressive account acquisition in recent periods that could drive elevated bad debt charges into FY2026.

findings.title: FY2024 Base Distorted by R1.02bn Non-Cash Trademark Impairment Reversal
findings.description: Headline earnings per share (HEPS) fell 8.0% (752.1c vs 817.9c), but unadjusted basic EPS plummeted 28.8% (745.2c vs 1,046.9c) and Group profit for the period dropped 28.3% (R2,796m vs R3,900m). The prior year result was heavily flattered by an exceptional R1,019 million pre-tax non-cash reversal of intangible asset (Office UK trademark) impairments, plus R134m in ROU asset impairment reversals. In Note 35.1, Office UK trading profit dropped from R2,398m to R1,363m, giving the illusion of an operational collapse if the non-operating impairment reversal is not stripped out.
findings.source_section: Note 31 Earnings and cash flow per share and Note 35 Segment Reporting
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: Profit for the period, attributable to equity holders of the company 2,790 (2024: 3,887) ... Impairment reversal of trademarks - (2024: (1,012)) ... Headline earnings 2,816 (2024: 3,037)
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: EBITDA, operating margin normalization, and earnings growth baseline
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Ensure valuation models base historical growth rates on normalized trading operating profit and headline earnings rather than IFRS basic operating profit, which was inflated by R1,019m in FY2024.

findings.title: Material Overhead Cost Inflation in Administration and Uncapitalized Store Leases
findings.description: Operating expenses expanded ahead of sales growth. Administration expenses within other operating costs rose 30.1% from R469 million to R610 million. Total occupancy costs not capitalized under IFRS 16 jumped 6.8% to R1,145 million, driven by a 67.3% surge in turnover-based lease expenses (R82m vs R49m) and a 10.1% increase in short-term lease expenses (R239m vs R217m). Furthermore, net finance costs escalated 10.3% from R476m to R525m due to rising lease liability interest (R306m vs R288m) and higher overdraft usage (R71m vs R61m).
findings.source_section: Note 27.4 Occupancy costs and Note 27.6 Other operating costs
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: Administration costs 610 (2024: 469) ... Turnover-based lease expenses 82 (2024: 49) ... Total lease expenses 321 (2024: 266) ... Finance costs: Lease liabilities 306 (2024: 288) ... Total 525 (2024: 476)
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Operating expenditure growth rate, SG&A as percentage of sales, and net interest expense
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Model higher recurring general administrative expenses and variable lease terms; verify whether short-term and turnover-based leases will reset higher in renewing mall contracts.

findings.title: Zero Depreciation Recognized on Newly Completed Distribution Centre Building
findings.description: Truworths completed the construction of its new 50/50 joint operation Distribution Centre (TDC Airport) and took full occupation under a 15-year lease starting December 2023. At year-end, TREIC had capitalised R171 million in construction costs. Note 34 notes that zero depreciation has been recognised against the building because management asserts its 'residual value exceeds the cost thereof'. Truworths Ltd also capitalized R722 million into plant and equipment for materials handling equipment.
findings.source_section: Note 34 Distribution Centre
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: At the reporting date TREIC had incurred and capitalised construction and related costs in the amount of R171 million. No depreciation has been recognised as the residual value of the building exceeds the cost thereof. ... Truworths Ltd has entered into a separate agreement with another service provider to supply and install the materials handling equipment. At the reporting date R722 million had been incurred and capitalised to plant and equipment.
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Depreciation and amortisation run-rate, PP&E carrying values, and operating expenses
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Evaluate the sensitivity of depreciation expense to the residual value assumption of the distribution centre. Assess the incremental depreciation charge coming into full effect for the R722m materials handling equipment in FY2026.

findings.title: Dividend Retrenchment (-7.9%) Reflecting Constrained Cash Allocation
findings.description: Total dividends declared per share declined 7.9% from 529 cents to 487 cents, with the final cash dividend cut by 13.7% from 197 cents to 170 cents per share. This cash dividend reduction reflects lower earnings and ongoing capital commitments (R632m capex, R1,105m lease principal repayments, and R1,500m short-term borrowings maturities within 365 days).
findings.source_section: Note 30 Dividends
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: Dividends per share: Final cash dividend - payable/paid September 170 (2024: 197) ... Interim cash dividend - paid March 317 (2024: 332) ... Total 487 (2024: 529)
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Dividend payout ratio and projected dividend yield
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Reduce projected dividend growth in the forecast horizon to align with headline earnings growth and elevated debt repayment/capex requirements.

findings.title: Severe R5.8bn Revaluation Deficit on Domestic Retail Subsidiaries
findings.description: At the standalone company level, Truworths recorded an other comprehensive loss of R5.811bn driven by a massive downward revaluation of direct retail subsidiaries, turning total comprehensive income to a loss of R2.125bn (down from a gain of R12.905bn in FY2024). Specifically, the fair value of Truworths Ltd (the core South African retail arm) was written down by R7.721bn (-28.8%) from R26.796bn to R19.075bn, and Young Designers Emporium (YDE) was written down by 57.9% from R377.6m to R158.9m. Because these are valued using EV/EBITDA multiples and DCFs, this sharp contraction signals peer multiple de-rating and compressed medium-term earnings expectations for domestic operations.
findings.source_section: Company Statements of Comprehensive Income / Note 2 & Note 8.6.2
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: Revaluation of subsidiaries: (5,814,813) [2024: 10,542,977] ... Total comprehensive (loss)/income for the period: (2,125,219) [2024: 12,905,241] ... Shares in Truworths Ltd: Balance at the beginning of the period: 26,795,961; Revaluation recognised in other comprehensive income: (7,720,626); Balance at the reporting date: 19,075,335
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Subsidiary carrying values, NAV per share, long-term terminal multiple and growth expectations for SA retail
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Analyze underlying EV/EBITDA multiples applied to Truworths Ltd and verify whether consensus forward EBITDA or multiple derating drove the R7.72bn cut in fair value.

findings.title: Progressive Cut in Dividend Distributions (DPS down 8.0% YoY)
findings.description: The dividend declared per share continues to deteriorate across FY2025. The final dividend declared on 28 August 2025 was cut to 170 cents per share (FY2024 final: 197 cps; FY2023 final: 245 cps), representing a 13.7% YoY decline and a 30.6% cut versus FY2023. Combined with the interim dividend of 317 cps (down from 332 cps in FY2024), total full-year dividends declared dropped to 487 cps from 529 cps in FY2024 and 565 cps in FY2023, reflecting constrained cash generation and defensive liquidity positioning.
findings.source_section: Note 12: Dividends
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: The final dividend for the period ended 29 June 2025 of 170 cents per share, before deduction of dividends tax (where applicable), was declared on 28 August 2025 ... Total dividends declared: 2,099,685 [2024: 2,357,038]
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Dividend yield, dividend payout ratio, free cash flow generation forecast
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Adjust dividend forecast models downwards to reflect the 487 cps full-year payout and assess impact on total shareholder return assumptions.

findings.title: Substantial Executive Equity Liquidations Post-Vesting
findings.description: Annexure Two reveals heavy disposal of vested executive equity awards during FY2025. Executive directors sold 451k shares/options upon vesting, exceeding the 398k retained. Specifically, CEO Michael Mark exercised and sold 301,000 PSP shares on 30 September 2024 at an exit price of R107.31 (generating ~R32.3m in gross proceeds). Similarly, Sarah Proudfoot disposed of 104k PSP shares and 5k options at prices between R72.15 and R107.31. This elevated rate of executive monetization near cyclical share price highs raises questions regarding insider confidence in multi-year growth runway.
findings.source_section: Annexure Two: Details of Directors' Holdings of Shares and Equity-Based Awards
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: Awards vested, exercised and sold: (451) [2024: (1,296)] ... Michael Mark: Vested and sold during the period: (301) ... On 30 September 2024, market price 107.31
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Management alignment, insider trading sentiment, governance risk premium
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Monitor net changes in director beneficial shareholdings relative to long-term incentive plan issuance and track ongoing director disposal activity.

findings.title: Parent Guarantee Exposure to External Subsidiary Borrowings and Real Estate Entity
findings.description: Truworths International Ltd acts as guarantor for external debt facilities contracted by Truworths Ltd and K2022434602 (South Africa) (Pty) Ltd (the 50% joint property holding company for the new distribution centre). While headline holding company liabilities are low (R12m), the parent balance sheet is directly exposed to external credit default risk and financial covenants of operating subsidiaries and joint property development ventures.
findings.source_section: Note 7: Financial Guarantees
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: The company is a guarantor for the external borrowings of Truworths Ltd and K2022434602 (SOUTH AFRICA) (Pty) Ltd (t/a Truworths Real Estate Investment Company).
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Contingent liabilities, holding company credit rating, debt recourse
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Verify external borrowing levels, maturity dates, and debt covenant terms inside K2022434602 and Truworths Ltd covered by the parent guarantee.

findings.title: Inter-Company Paper Settlement of Historical Share Buy-Back Indebtedness
findings.description: In FY2024, the holding company carried an inter-company liability of R1.588bn owing to Truworths Ltd, which financed prior-period share repurchases. During FY2025, this entire liability was extinguished through a non-cash accounting set-off against inter-company dividend income declared by Truworths Ltd (R1.583bn non-cash movement). Consequently, of the R3.688bn headline dividend income reported in profit before tax, only R2.101bn was received in actual operating cash flows, distorting cash earnings quality at the parent level.
findings.source_section: Note 6: Loans and Other Payables & Note 13.6
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: The amount owing to Truworths Ltd in the prior period related mainly to financial assistance provided by Truworths Ltd to the company for the purpose of share buy-backs in prior periods, and was settled in the current period through off-set against a dividend declared by Truworths Ltd on inter-company loan account. ... Truworths Ltd: Balance at the beginning (1,587,898), Non-cash movements: 1,583,255, Balance at the reporting date: (4,643)
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Holding company cash conversion ratio, inter-company financing liquidity
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Separate paper dividend income from actual operating cash upstreaming when assessing corporate dividend capacity and share buy-back headroom.

findings.title: Gross Margin Contraction and Negative Operating Leverage
findings.description: Cost of sales increased by 5% (R10,389m vs R9,859m) while merchandise sales grew only 3% (R21,323m vs R20,664m), driving a 100 bps contraction in gross margin from 52.3% to 51.3%. Compounding this, occupancy costs grew 7% (R1,145m vs R1,072m) and finance costs rose 10% (R525m vs R476m), illustrating that structural operating expenses and cost inflation outpaced top-line growth.
findings.source_section: Pro Forma Information
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Gross margin, trading margin, and operating leverage assumptions
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Adjust forecast gross profit margins downward by 100 bps and model higher operating expense escalations; stress-test operational leverage under sub-5% revenue growth.

findings.title: Underlying Earnings Decline Masked by Prior-Year Office UK Trademark Reversal
findings.description: Reported FY2024 base figures were substantially elevated by non-operational one-offs, notably a R1,019m Office UK trademark impairment reversal, R122m net ROU asset impairment reversal, and R123m benefit from charitable trust consolidation. While reported basic EPS fell 29% (from 1,046.9c to 745.2c), even on an adjusted/pro forma basis, HEPS declined 4% (from 780.8c to 752.1c) and reported HEPS fell 8% (from 817.9c to 752.1c), exposing genuine operational margin deterioration across both trading and operating profit lines.
findings.source_section: Pro Forma Information - Basis of preparation
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: The Group’s prior period earnings were enhanced by the following once-off events/transactions, making the prior period reported figures less comparable to the current period (and hence the pro forma adjustments): • a trademark impairment reversal in relation to the Office UK trademark (R1 019 million); • a net right of use asset impairment reversal (R122 million)... • a reduction in other operating costs (R123 million) resulting from the consolidation of the Group's charitable trusts
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Normalized EPS growth rate and high-base earnings adjustments
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Ensure base-year normalization removes the R1,019m trademark reversal and associated deferred tax when projecting forward growth; verify that consensus reflects real underlying negative earnings momentum.

findings.title: High Shareholder and Management Fund Concentration via South African State Pension Funds
findings.description: Significant institutional shareholder concentration exists: Government Employees Pension Fund holds 21.5% (87,993,401 shares) and Public Investment Corporation administers 18.9% (77,180,224 shares) of issued share capital. In total, the top 73 shareholders control 72.4% of total shares, leaving free-float and secondary market liquidity highly sensitive to state pension asset allocation shifts.
findings.source_section: Shareholder Information - Holders of Major Beneficial Interests in Shares
findings.evidence_quote_or_span: Government Employees Pension Fund South Africa 87,993,401 21.5% ... Public Investment Corporation South Africa 77,180,224 18.9% ... Over 1 000 000 [holding size] 73 [shareholdings] 295,895,972 [shares] 72.4%
findings.affected_metric_or_assumption: Share liquidity risk premium and cost of equity
findings.recommended_analyst_review: Monitor domestic South African asset manager reallocations and sovereign fund mandate changes that could create significant overhang.
